excerpt: SecurityScorecard rates the cybersecurity of companies and their suppliers from the outside, with A–F grades, and sells third-party risk management tools. Free account available.
content:
SecurityScorecard is a cybersecurity company best known for security ratings. It looks at signals about an organisation's security that can be observed from outside, across several security dimensions, and turns them into a letter grade from A to F. TechCrunch explained in 2021 that the grades work like school grades and that any company can see its own scorecard for free, with suggestions for improving it. Businesses use the ratings to monitor the vendors and suppliers they depend on, which is known as third-party or supply chain risk management, and its website also lists cyber insurance as a use case.

Its current platform is called TITAN AI. The website lists packages named TITAN Watch for monitoring, TITAN Assess for security questionnaires, TITAN Secure for threat-informed findings and response, and TITAN MAX managed services, alongside threat intelligence and AI agents. The site says more than 25,000 organisations use SecurityScorecard.

CEO Aleksandr Yampolskiy and COO Sam Kassoumeh co-founded the company. Yampolskiy told TechCrunch the idea came from his time as a CISO and CTO, when he had no metrics to judge security.

Funding

On 18 March 2021 SecurityScorecard announced a $180 million Series E. New investors included Silver Lake Waterman, T. Rowe Price, Kayne Anderson Rudnick and Fitch Ventures, with existing backers including Evolution Equity Partners, Riverwood Capital, Intel Capital and GV. SiliconANGLE put total funding at about $292 million after the round.

Pricing

SecurityScorecard does not publish prices. Its pricing page offers a Free Forever account with a rating for your own domain, self-monitoring and basic reports, and a free trial of TITAN Watch; paid packages are priced mainly on how many organisations you monitor.

We have not tested SecurityScorecard. This page is based on its website and pricing page (checked 15 October 2026), TechCrunch and SiliconANGLE.
